cross_component_finding: This page defines DDL/DCL/DML as the three top-level SQL++ statement categories ('Data Definition Language (DDL) statements enable you to create and modify database objects... Data Control Language (DCL) statements enable you to control which users or groups have access to data... Data Manipulation Language (DML) statements enable you to create, read, update, and delete data'). This categorization scheme is not yet modeled in the registry as a concept scheme (unlike index-state or cluster-access-credential-type), and no other page in this 12-page batch states it explicitly, so it is not minted here - flagging for the reconciler in case it recurs with enough frequency across the fuller corpus to warrant an n1ql:statement-category scheme. Separately, this page states 'The Couchbase implementation of SQL++ was formerly known as [N1QL]' - a product-branding/rename fact, not modeled as a relation to avoid conflating it with the unrelated cbl: namespace's own SQL++ dialect concepts.
